per_agent.pseudo: A heat wave strips the last pretense of universal access from the electrical grid: the machines that were built to cool every household trip offline, and the rationing that follows is never symmetrical. In the great cities, the powerless sweat through a second dark night while the industrial lobbies — whose production lines never stop — press for emergency fuel, their voice carried to the table of decision with a force that the consumer group's demand for mere transparency will never match. Maintenance is deferred on the plants that serve the many; the price of that deferral is paid in sleep lost and food spoiled in tenement kitchens, not in quarterly filings.

They built their cities upon the certainty of flame — and for a time the flame obeyed. But the hour arrived, as it was always foreordained to arrive, when the heat of the heavens pressed down and the servants of fire lay themselves down and would not rise. The towers went dark, and those within them cried out against those who had kept the schedules of maintenance in sealed books. The merchants pleaded for more fuel to be carried from distant lands, as though the problem were merely distance and not the ancient covenant broken between those who consume and the element that grants itself only so long as it is honored.

Hundreds of millions of fans spin to a halt across great cities, and no one can explain it fully for days. It all began with a single filter gauge, mounted on one fossil-fuel unit, whose reading had drifted three decimal points too low over eleven months because a maintenance schedule — printed on paper — sat one shelf above where the technician habitually looked. He checked the wrong page every time. When the heat wave arrived, that unattended unit tripped first; the others followed like dominoes no one had bothered to test in sequence. By nightfall entire boroughs rationed electricity, and somewhere a crumpled maintenance log was quietly thrown away.

During a period of extreme heat, several fuel-burning power units shut down automatically as demand reaches record levels. The regional grid operator issues a warning: rolling outages are expected. For two consecutive nights, utilities rotate and reduce electricity supply across major cities to prevent a wider collapse. Consumer groups request public disclosure of plant maintenance schedules. Industrial groups ask governments to authorize emergency fuel shipments. Demand remains high as temperatures stay elevated. Grid crews monitor load balances and switch supply between regions on timed rotations through the night.

candidates.title: Out of Inferno
candidates.overview: On the hottest day in 50 years, a serious fire incident happened to a busy commercial tower, a gaggle of fire fighters with an indestructible enthusiasm are going to save lives.

candidates.title: Pyromaniac
candidates.overview: In the darkness of a peaceful village, a pyromaniac ignites his first fire. As more fires break out, the society panics. An inferno lurks under the surface as a local policeman uncovers the unthinkable truth...

candidates.title: Survival Family
candidates.overview: A world wide electrical outage occurs. Everything that requires electricity comes to a stop. Tokyo is nearly ruined. Yoshiyuki Suzuki decides to escape from Tokyo with his family.

candidates.title: The Black Hole
candidates.overview: It's 2 A.M. in St. Louis when a routine scientific experiment goes terribly wrong and an explosion shakes the city. A scientific team investigates, clashing with an intergalactic, voltage-devouring creature that vaporizes them.

candidates.title: The Steam Experiment
candidates.overview: A deranged scientist locks 6 people in a steam room and threatens to turn up the heat if the local paper doesn't publish his story about global warming.

candidates.title: Pan 1
candidates.overview: A pendulum swings by until it comes to a complete stop.

candidates.title: I Told You So
candidates.overview: In Rome, during a January weekend a sudden heatwave arrives. The sun is initially pleasant, but the heat quickly escalates to a frightening degree, resulting in people and animals losing self-control.

candidates.title: Gasland
candidates.overview: It is happening all across America-rural landowners wake up one day to find a lucrative offer from an energy company wanting to lease their property. Reason? The company hopes to tap into a reservoir dubbed the "Saudi Arabia of natural gas." Halliburton developed a way to get the gas out of the ground-a hydraulic drilling process called "fracking"-and suddenly America finds itself on the precipice of becoming an energy superpower.
